title: The Chern class of a normalized supported Kummer boundary
statement: Let T be a scheme, A a commutative ring with N=0 in A, N invertible on T, and i:D→T an effective Cartier closed immersion. If κ in Ext²(i_*A_D,A_T(1)) satisfies SupportedKummerBoundary of [def-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer-boundary], then forgetting coefficients and precomposing with the supported integral generator and integral constant unit of [def-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer-boundary] gives the positive Kummer Chern class of the dual Cartier ideal.

source.place: Paragraphs 3--4: forgetting the relative trivialization gives the first Chern class

proof.text: Choose a torsor-extension witness of the boundary specification. Sending a frame p to its image f(p) in the extension identifies the frame torsor with the lifting torsor above supported one: hb gives the fibre condition, naturality of f gives restriction, and hf gives equivariance. By the torsor/H¹ comparison, its class is the connecting boundary of supported one.

The Picard class of the dual ideal is the class of its frame torsor. The degree-zero cohomology/section adjunction identifies evaluation of the integral constant one under a morphism f with Ext.mk₀ f. Apply the Kummer connecting morphism and the root coefficient map. The boundary normalization equation and associativity then give the Chern identity with the underived integral supported unit.

theorem supported_kummer_chern_realization (T : Scheme.{u}) (N : ℕ)
    (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A] (hA : (N : A) = 0)
    (hT : IsUnit (N : Γ(T, ⊤))) {D : Scheme.{u}} (i : D ⟶ T)
    [IsClosedImmersion i] (hI : i.ker.IsInvertible)
    (κ : Ext ((lowerStar (ModuleCat.{u + 1} A) i).obj (ordinaryFiniteConstant A D))
      (Scheme.finiteEtaleTateLine T N A hA) 2)
    (hκ : SupportedKummerBoundary A N hA i hI hT κ) :
    (Ext.mk₀ (supportedIntegralUnit i)).comp
      ((Ext.mk₀ (supportedIntegralGenerator A i)).comp
        (κ.mapExactFunctor (RawModuleScalarComparison.forget A T)) (zero_add 2))
      (zero_add 2) = supportedKummerChern A N hA i hI hT
